# User Stories — SPEC-013 Parallel Dispatch (M1)

Plain-language summaries of the seven user stories that shaped this feature. Each summary
describes who benefits, what the story delivers, and which acceptance criteria govern it.

---

## US-001 — Wave Scheduler Core Procedure

**Who uses this.** A pipeline operator running a large spec in multi-task mode — for example, a
spec with a dozen independent backend tasks spread across multiple user stories.

**What it does.** This story authors `procedures/ship-step2-dag-dispatch.md`, a new nine-section
procedure that the orchestrator follows to schedule tasks in waves. The procedure specifies every
step the orchestrator must execute: reading and normalizing task write-sets, detecting dependency
cycles, classifying tasks against a hardcoded Node/TS lock list, greedily selecting a disjoint
wave, dispatching K `Agent` tool-calls with worktree isolation, symlinking shared `node_modules`
into each worktree, and merging only declared files back to the main tree after each agent
returns.

Before M1, if task A and task B both touched different files and belonged to different user
stories, they would still wait in a queue and run one (or at most two, within the same US)
at a time. After M1, the scheduler computes that A and B are write-disjoint, places them in the
same wave, and hands them off together in a single orchestrator turn.

**Acceptance criteria.** The procedure must exist and must specify: the cycle-guard (fail-fast
fatal on any dependency cycle, no dispatch); deterministic greedy wave selection (sort by task id,
add a task iff its write-set is disjoint from all already-added members and the wave is under cap,
guarantee a floor of 1 even when all candidates conflict); the inlined Node/TS lock list
(`package.json`, lockfiles, `**/index.ts`, `**/index.js`, `prisma/schema.prisma`,
`**/migrations/**`); worktree dispatch with `isolation: "worktree"`; dep-sharing via `node_modules`
symlinks; and file-scoped merge that keeps task `.md` status fields and `.run-manifest.jsonl`
exclusively in the main tree.

**Tasks.** T-001 authored the scheduler algorithm (cycle detection, wave selection, lock list).
T-002 extended it with the dep-sharing symlink sequence and file-scoped merge protocol.

## US-002 — Ship Step 2 Rewrite and Startup Reconcile

**Who uses this.** Any pipeline operator running `/ship` in multi-task mode — the scheduler
procedure from US-001 means nothing if `commands/ship.md` Step 2 does not actually call it.

**What it does.** This story rewrites `commands/ship.md` Step 2 to branch on `DISPATCH_MODE`:
when `multi-task`, it delegates to the wave scheduler procedure instead of the old per-US
sequential walk; when `per-task` or `single-task`, the existing paths are untouched.

It also adds Step 1.10 to the `/ship` startup sequence: an idempotent worktree reconcile that
runs `git worktree prune` and then sweeps any leftover branches matching the `planr-wt/*` prefix
before the dispatch queue is built. If a previous `/ship` run crashed mid-wave, orphaned
worktrees and stale branches accumulate; the reconcile step removes them automatically on the
next run so the scheduler starts from a clean state.

**Acceptance criteria.** In `multi-task` mode, Step 2 delegates to the new procedure. The
`per-task` and `single-task` branches are byte-for-byte unchanged. The reconcile step runs
`git worktree prune`, enumerates `planr-wt/*` branches, deletes them, and logs what it removed.
The `--max-parallel` value is read from `$SHIP_MAX_PARALLEL` (bound in Phase A of the
arguments-and-cost-gate procedure) and passed to the scheduler. The `--all-tasks` flag
composes with `--max-parallel` without implying unbounded width.

**Tasks.** T-003 rewrote the Step 2 multi-task branch. T-004 added the Step 1.10 reconcile.

Note: the task spec named the reconcile step "Step 1.9" but the pre-existing Step 1.9 (project
memory read) was already in `commands/ship.md`. The implementation correctly numbers it Step 1.10.
The QA report records this as a non-blocking label mismatch in the task spec only.

## US-003 — `--max-parallel` Argument Parsing and Validation

**Who uses this.** A pipeline operator who wants to control how many tasks are handed off per
wave, either to manage rate limits, limit orchestrator context size, or opt out of fan-out
entirely by setting the width to 1.

**What it does.** This story extends `procedures/ship-arguments-and-cost-gate.md` Phase A to
parse `--max-parallel N`, validate it strictly, and bind the result as `$SHIP_MAX_PARALLEL`
for downstream use by the scheduler.

Validation follows the same pattern as the existing `--task` flag. A missing flag defaults
silently to 4. A value of 1 through 20 is accepted silently. A value above 20 triggers a
soft one-line warning about rate limits and orchestrator context blast radius (a wave of K tasks
returns K result summaries into the orchestrator's context in one turn), but the run continues.
A value of 0, a negative number, or a non-numeric token produces a two-line fatal in
`procedures/fatal-error-format.md` style and halts dispatch immediately.

**Acceptance criteria.** The Phase A flag table includes `--max-parallel`. The default is 4.
Invalid values produce two-line fatals. Values above 20 produce a soft warning and continue.
The value 1 is accepted silently and produces sequential-equivalent dispatch (verified by the G4
conformance fixture in US-005). The bound output `$SHIP_MAX_PARALLEL` is explicitly referenced
by `commands/ship.md` Step 2b-multi.

**Tasks.** T-005 added the parsing and validation block to Phase A.

## US-004 — Undeclared-Write QA Rule DRY Consolidation and Proof Right-Sizing

**Who uses this.** A pipeline maintainer who needs the "a task may not write a file outside its
declared Create/Modify list" rule to be canonical and consistent across all QA consumers.

**What it does.** Before this story, the undeclared-write rejection policy was described
independently in `agents/qa-agent.md`, `agents/modes/default/qa.md`, and
`agents/modes/spec-driven/qa.md`. Three copies of the same rule create drift risk.

This story moves the normative policy to `agents/modes/shared/contract-create-modify-preserve.md`
as Rule 4, then replaces the three independent copies with a single cross-reference line pointing
to Rule 4. Rule 4 states: any file changed in a worktree that is absent from both the Create and
Modify lists is an undeclared write; the orchestrator will reject it at merge time and fail the
task into R6; the undeclared file must not land in main.

The story also right-sizes the conformance runner's assertion wording. Before this work, some
assertion text implied that overlapping `.run-manifest.jsonl` timestamps prove wall-clock
concurrency. The orchestrator writes those timestamps, so overlap proves batching intent at most,
not that two agents were running simultaneously on real CPU time. The corrected assertions claim
only "clobber-prevention end-state" and "structural batching" — what M1 can actually prove.

**Acceptance criteria.** Rule 4 exists in the shared contract. No independent copy of the rule
exists in the three QA files. `conformance/runner.mjs` contains no assertion message that claims
"overlapping intervals = concurrency". The undeclared-write conformance fixture (Fixture-C) still
fails tasks through Rule 4 after the consolidation.

**Tasks.** T-006 wrote Rule 4 and replaced the QA file copies with cross-references. T-007
right-sized the conformance runner assertion wording.

## US-005 — G4 Critical Regression Fixture: `--max-parallel 1` Equals Sequential Dispatch

**Who uses this.** A pipeline operator who relied on the previous sequential dispatch behavior and
wants to verify that `--max-parallel 1` is a true escape hatch — not merely "slower", but
byte-for-byte identical to what the pipeline produced before M1.

**What it does.** This story creates two conformance fixtures: G4 and G3.

G4 is the iron-rule regression fixture. It seeds a two-task spec, runs it at `--max-parallel 1`,
and asserts that the dispatch order, interval non-overlap, and id-ascending task ordering all
match the pre-M1 sequential behavior exactly. If this fixture ever fails, it means the wave
scheduler at width 1 produces different output from the legacy sequential walk, which would
break any operator relying on the flag as an opt-out.

G3 covers argument validation end-to-end: three two-line fatals (for 0, -3, and `abc`), the
blast-radius warning for a value of 50, and silent accept for a value of 1 (no spurious warning).

**Acceptance criteria.** Both fixture directories exist under `conformance/fixtures/`. The
runner asserts G4 (10 assertions) and G3 (21 assertions). All seven previously-shipped spec
fixtures replay green at width 1. The G4 fixture explicitly references `--max-parallel 1`.

**Tasks.** T-008 created both fixtures and wired the runner assertions.

## US-006 — Conformance Coverage Fixtures: Crash Recovery and Wave-Behavior Scenarios

**Who uses this.** A pipeline contributor who needs automated regression coverage for the key
behaviors of the wave scheduler beyond what G4 and G3 cover.

**What it does.** This story creates six more conformance fixtures and their runner assertions:

- **G1 (multi-wave)**: a four-task write-disjoint spec with cap 2 resolves in exactly 2 waves
  (`ceil(4/2) = 2`), id-ascending within each wave.
- **G2 (floor-of-1)**: three tasks that all share the same file (mutually conflicting) resolve as
  three sequential waves of 1. The floor-of-1 invariant — the scheduler never produces an empty
  wave while the queue is non-empty — is asserted explicitly.
- **G6 (crash recovery)**: a half-merged state seeded with T-001 done, T-002 in-progress (stale
  worktree branch present), T-003 pending. Re-running `/ship` must skip T-001, re-queue T-002,
  prune the stale `planr-wt/` branch, and never double-merge T-001.
- **G7 (merge scope)**: a worktree diff that contains both a declared `src/feature.ts` and the
  task's own `.md` file. Only `src/feature.ts` must land in main; the task `.md` must be withheld.
- **Fixture-A (clobber prevention)**: two tasks with overlapping write-sets are serialized into
  different waves; the second task's version of the shared file is the final state (`version-B`).
- **Fixture-C (undeclared write)**: a task whose worktree diff contains an undeclared path is
  blocked entirely — nothing from the worktree lands in main, and an error-report citing
  `contract-create-modify-preserve.md` Rule 4 is written.
- **Fixture-D (cyclic dependency)**: a three-task overlap graph triggers the cycle guard. The
  fixture asserts a two-line fatal, zero dispatch, zero manifest records, and exit code 2.

**Acceptance criteria.** All six fixture directories exist. The runner asserts each scenario.
The undeclared-write fixture passes through Rule 4 (verifying the US-004 DRY consolidation).
No assertion claims overlapping intervals prove wall-clock concurrency.

**Tasks.** T-009 created G6 (crash recovery). T-010 created G1, G2, G7, Fixture-A, Fixture-C,
Fixture-D.

## US-007 — Docs Update: Wave Dispatch and Safety Model

**Who uses this.** A contributor or operator reading the planr-pipeline reference documentation
who needs accurate descriptions of the wave-dispatch model, worktree isolation, and the impact
on each runtime adapter.

**What it does.** This story updates four existing documentation files to reflect M1:

- `docs/protocol/runtime-adapters.md` previously described wave-member subagents writing to the
  shared main tree. The update adds a "Worktree Isolation (multi-task mode)" subsection under
  the Claude Code adapter section, clarifying that worktree isolation is a host primitive
  (`isolation: "worktree"` on the `Agent` tool), is multi-task-mode-only, and names the branch
  and directory conventions.
- `docs/rules.md` receives R11 "Wave Write-Safety (multi-task mode only)" as a new hard rule.
  R11 states the disjoint write-set + lock-list requirement, the empty-write-set serialization
  rule, the worktree isolation requirement, and the file-scoped merge requirement, scoped
  explicitly to `DISPATCH_MODE: multi-task`.
- `docs/pipeline-overview.md` receives a "Parallel Dispatch (M1)" section that describes wave
  structure, the three-layer write-safety model, the `--max-parallel` cap, and the
  sequential-parity escape hatch. It explicitly states that a wave does not promise wall-clock
  concurrency — it bounds how many tasks the orchestrator hands off at once.
- `docs/compatibility-matrix.md` receives a "DAG-aware parallel dispatch" row and subsection
  documenting that full fan-out is Claude Code only; Cursor and Codex remain per-task sequential
  and are unaffected by SPEC-013.

**Acceptance criteria.** Each of the four files contains the described additions. The
compatibility matrix is accurate about the multi-task-only scope. None of the updated files
claims wall-clock concurrency as a guaranteed property.

**Tasks.** T-011 updated all four documentation files in a single task (disjoint write-set from
all other SPEC-013 tasks, dispatched as the last lane per the design doc's parallelization
strategy).
